assumptions: Frame: heliocentric ICRF/J2000 axes, Sun centre (as idea 39 and Aster); time TDB seconds past J2000, UTC = TDB - 69.184 s, UT1 = UTC.

Forces: the Sun (GM 132712440018000000000, Aster), the Earth (GM 398600441800000, Aster; J2 0.00108262539 about the ICRF z axis, DE440), the Moon and Mercury..Neptune system barycentres (DE440 GMs), the Sun's Schwarzschild term (c 299792458 m/s); planets by Chebyshev fits of JPL Horizons (Aster's daily file and fetched records); no asteroid perturbers, no non-gravitational forces on the target.
Integrator: Dormand-Prince 5(4), relative tolerance 1e-12; the state transition matrix integrated from the point-mass gravity gradient (J2, relativity and sunlight left out of it).

Navigation: linear covariance analysis; Doppler every 2 h of a pass, one range point per pass, Delta-DOR on two baselines; stations turned by the Earth rotation angle only; light time ignored; data cut off 3 days before each TCM.
TCMs: impulsive, fixed-time position targeting of the arrival; statistics from 4000 seeded samples of N(deterministic, G P G^T); execution errors by Gates' model.

assumptions: Frames: body-fixed APOPHIS_CK (NAIF -2099942000) for the field and the surface, origin moved 5.67 m to the uniform-density centre of mass; orbits in ICRF axes about the centre of mass. Time TDB s past J2000, UTC = TDB - 69.184 s.
Gravity: the constant-density polyhedron of Apophis RAD v001 (NAIF DSK surface 425000001) (3996 plates), G = 6.6743e-11 (NIST), density 2025.3 kg/m^3 = GM / (G V).
Spin: torque-free rotation with Pravec et al. (2014)'s inertia ratios from NAIF's CK sample nearest the epoch.

Surface: each plate's centroid; acceleration = gravity minus the spin's centrifugal and Euler terms; slope = angle between the inward normal and that acceleration; height = (geopotential - its area mean) / local acceleration; escape speeds from energy in a non-rotating field (sqrt(2U)), straight up and along the spin.

Orbits: the scan flies gravity alone (no sunlight, no tide), circular starts at sqrt(GM/r) on the node of the spin equator; Orbital B adds idea 42's sunlight and solar tide, tabulated along the reconstruction (area per mass 1/81.119 m^2/kg, OSIRIS-APEX).

assumptions: Frames: flight in ICRF axes about the centre of mass; the site, ground-relative velocities and heights in the body frame of idea 43's shape (APOPHIS_CK (NAIF -2099942000)). Time TDB s past J2000; UTC = TDB - 69.184 s.

Gravity: idea 43's constant-density polyhedron (3996 plates, density 2025.3 kg/m^3), turning with the body; sunlight: idea 42's 7.765e-8 m/s^2 along the Sun line, off in the body's shadow cylinder; the solar tide (~1e-11 m/s^2 here) left out.

Burns: impulsive. Profile after OSIRIS-REx (Berry et al. 2020): departure, Checkpoint 125 m above the aim point along the site normal 24.00 h later, Matchpoint 10.0 min after that, contact 10.0 min after Matchpoint; the Checkpoint and Matchpoint burns target the contact point and a contact velocity of 10 cm/s along the normal with no horizontal speed relative to the ground (the Matchpoint height is an outcome); the spacecraft's reference point 3.4 m (the TAGSAM arm) above the site at contact.

Dispersions: linear covariance from Checkpoint, onboard knowledge 1 m / 1 mm/s (3 sigma per axis) and Berry et al. 2021 Table 2 execution errors (late columns, read as 3 sigma), scaled by 1; gravity, sunlight and attitude errors are not included.
Contact: the head (32 cm base plate) meets a constant resistance; the arm's constant-force spring, the gas jet and tipping are not modelled.

assumptions: Frames and time: the Sun direction from JPL Horizons (ICRF axes, TDB), turned into idea 43's body frame (APOPHIS_CK, NAIF CK samples with Euler's equations); the site normal is idea 44's plate 346. UTC = TDB - 69.184 s.

Sunlight: 1361.2 W/m^2 at 1 au (idea 40's solar luminosity over 4 pi au^2), scaled by (1 au / r)^2; a Sun-tracking concentrator works while the Sun is more than 0 deg above the site plane; the oven is shut in the dark (no heat lost at night, none kept).

Heat: Hess's law over Robie and Hemingway (1995): the water as chrysotile breaking down to forsterite + enstatite + steam, the rest of the rock as forsterite; the steam leaves at the oven temperature; no heat recovered; CO2, SO2 and organics leave too (their heats of reaction left out).
Oven: batches of 25 kg heated at the run's rate (10 K/min), 73 min each, only while lit; cavity emissivity 1, concentration 300, optical efficiency 0.85 (design choices, not data).

Digging: 1 pair(s) of IPEx small drums, counter-rotating (imbalance 0.1, assumed), 10.00 mm deep at 10 mm/s, tip 8.5x the cut speed (IPEx), only while lit; regolith 2025 kg/m^3 (idea 43's bulk density).
Robie and Hemingway's enstatite equation ends at 1000 K; the oven's 1023 K is 23 K beyond it (extrapolated).
